discovered-from:SA-0MV9JVLBQ0090RNC

## Problem

The audit merge gate (`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` → `_resolve_item_integration_evidence`) mines every hex token from the work item's description and comments and keeps those that resolve to **any** git object in the owning repo (`_commit_object_exists`). It does not filter by which ref the commit is reachable from.

When an item's text cites commits that exist only on `refs/worklog/data`, its backup refs, or other non-`dev` refs (e.g. a worklog history-rewrite item quoting incident-era SHAs), `_verify_merged_in_dev` finds no ancestor of `origin/dev` among the candidates and the gate proceeds to `_integrate_into_dev`, which cherry-picks those commits onto a worktree at `origin/dev` — conflicting and failing the audit closed with a spurious `Ready to close: No` merge-gate blocker.

## Observed (2026-10-23, SA-0MV9JVLBQ0090RNC)

- Audit run 1: `git cherry-pick 345ea154a -> rc=1` conflict; verdict `Ready to close: No` (merge-gate blocker). `345ea154a` is a `refs/worklog/data` commit, never a `dev` commit.
- Workaround applied: the item description now records a real `dev` commit (`92fee5c30`, an ancestor of `origin/dev`), so the ancestor scan short-circuits to merged before any cherry-pick. Fragile — it depends on authors remembering to cite a `dev` commit and on the scan order.
- Related (already completed): SA-0MTQAF62U0085BEV (foreign hex that is not an object at all) and SA-0MTECRNGR000VKLV (decimal literals mined as SHAs). This is a third variant: the token **is** a commit object, but not on the delivery ref.

## Desired behaviour

- Restrict integration-evidence candidates to commits reachable from the item's delivery surface (branches matching `wl-<id>-*`, and any commit that is an ancestor of `origin/dev` or of a referenced feature branch) — or, at minimum, skip candidates not reachable from any `refs/heads/*` / `origin/*` ref of the owning repo, recording the skip as evidence.
- Commits reachable only from `refs/worklog/*`, `refs/backup/*` or unreachable objects must never be cherry-picked onto `dev`.
- Keep fail-open behaviour for evidence-less items and fail-closed behaviour for genuinely unmerged feature work.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1:** A work item whose description cites commits reachable only from `refs/worklog/data` (or a backup ref) does NOT trigger `_integrate_into_dev`; the gate records a skip note naming each excluded candidate and its non-delivery ref.
2. **AC2:** Regression test (in `skill/audit/tests/`) builds a fixture repo with a `dev` branch, a `refs/worklog/data` commit and a description citing that commit, and asserts `_phase_merge_gate` passes without invoking cherry-pick (no stray worktree, no blocker).
3. **AC3:** Existing behaviour is unchanged for: the real delivered commit (ancestor of `origin/dev` → merged), genuinely unmerged feature-branch work (still integrates), and evidence-less items (fail-open).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MVY4SG8O001RSQF** – Fix: drive stranded-child commit evidence matches the work-item id in a commit body, producing a false stranded verdict (open)
- **SA-0MW3H07A8004Q54C** – finish: retry the local-dev fast-forward after the recovery rebase and report a pushed-commit-guard refusal distinctly (completed)
- **SA-0MW2A3WWQ008TDZV** – Implement skill: document the commit-bound pre-push gate (--gate-commit) as canonical-template behaviour (open)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: 0mtecrngr000vklv, 0mtqaf62u0085bev, ac1, ac2, ac3 (+120 more)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: 0mtecrngr000vklv, ac1, ac2, ac3, acceptance (+113 more)
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, acceptance, already (+108 more)
data.title: Audit merge gate treats commits on other refs (worklog/backup) as dev integration evidence

Discovered-from: SA-0MVE34D9B005TUYJ (claim-hold fix).

## Problem
acquireFileLock() (~/projects/ContextHub/src/file-lock.ts) removes a lock whose acquiredAt is older than DEFAULT_MAX_LOCK_AGE_MS (5 min) even when the holder PID is alive on the same host. A long wl sync (fetch/merge/push over a slow network or a large store) therefore has its lock stolen mid-operation, and two writers proceed concurrently: the sync then writes back its pre-operation snapshot over whatever the stealer committed (the general lost-update class that WL-0MUV2U9QF002S9J1 closed for short operations).

## Why it was not fixed in SA-0MVE34D9B005TUYJ
The claim-hold guard now prevents the user-visible damage (a reverted claim), but non-claim field writes are still exposed in that window.

## Suggested direction
Treat a same-host live holder as authoritative (no age-expiry), keep age-expiry for dead-PID / foreign-host / unparseable locks, and/or refresh the lock (acquiredAt heartbeat) during long syncs. Add a deterministic regression test using the sync-vs-mutation.test.ts git-shim parking technique plus a back-dated lock file.

## Key Files
- ~/projects/ContextHub/src/file-lock.ts
- ~/projects/ContextHub/src/commands/sync.ts
- ~/projects/ContextHub/tests/cli/sync-vs-mutation.test.ts
data.title: wl sync: file-lock age-expiry steals a live holder's lock (residual lost-update hazard)

## Goal

Once SA-0MVLJ8VD60091JLW makes `/proc/pressure` actually parse, the existing pressure thresholds need a calibration pass against real host data.

## Context

- `cpu_pressure` (70/85) is now applied to the `some` avg10 line — plausible, unvalidated.
- `io_pressure` (50/80) was chosen when the parser produced nothing and is applied to the `full` avg10 line; 50% full-stall is effectively never reached, so the metric would stay green under genuine I/O starvation.

## Acceptance criteria

- Thresholds for `cpu_pressure` and `io_pressure` are validated against observed stall percentages on a busy multi-agent host.
- `config.yaml` / `config.py::_DEFAULTS` / `SKILL.md` are updated consistently with the calibrated values and the rationale is recorded.
- Tests cover the new thresholds' classification boundaries.

## Notes

- discovered-from:SA-0MVLJ8VD60091JLW (scope-creep risk recorded there rather than widening that item).
- Related: ContextHub WL-0MVI8YM07002Z9VY (process/thread/swap threshold miscalibration).
data.title: machine-hygiene: recalibrate cpu_pressure/io_pressure thresholds now that PSI parsing works

Discovered while implementing SA-0MVHXWLPG007OQVN (drive timeout reconciliation).

Problem: when implement.py start runs from inside an already-existing worktree (the resume path used by every driven child session), Step 9 writes ImplementState.repo_root = str(Path.cwd().resolve()) — the worktree path, not the main checkout. phase_finish then calls _remove_worktree(worktree_path, repo_root=state.repo_root) whose safety gate 1 refuses when resolved_path == repo_root (CRITICAL: REFUSE to remove the repository root ... This is the main working tree, not a worktree; Restored status=open).

Impact: every driven child leaks its worktree, finish exits non-zero and restores the item to open even though the commit was pushed — a false failure needing manual status fix; .worklog/worktrees accumulates orphans.

Expected: phase_start should persist the main checkout root (e.g. via _main_checkout_for(worktree) following the gitdir) so phase_finish can remove the worktree after a successful push.

Evidence: SA-0MVLJWL60001H6QK finish (commit b11d0877d pushed to dev, finish reported failure, worktree left in place).
data.title: implement.py finish refuses to remove a resumed worktree because phase_start stores the worktree as repo_root

data.description:
Discovered by a full-project `/skill:refactor` scan of this repository (499 source files, clean `dev` checkout).

## User Story

**As a** producer running a refactor scan,
**I want** the report's "Auto-fixed" count to reflect changes actually written to disk,
**so that** I can trust the report and do not believe lint debt was cleaned when the tree is
byte-for-byte unchanged.

## Observed behaviour

`python3 skill/refactor/scripts/refactor.py` (no work-item id) reported:

```
Auto-fix applied 9 fixes via linters on 437 files
Auto-fixed:     9
Remaining smells: 9
```

but `git status` showed **no** source-file changes (only a pre-existing modification to
`.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json`), and a follow-up check confirmed the same 9 diagnostics
are still present:

```
$ ruff check --select SIM102,EXE005,ISC004,SIM115,UP031,SIM117,EXE001 \
    skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py skill/implement/scripts/implement.py \
    skill/shared/tests/test_wait_for_job.py skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_failure_notices.py \
    tests/test_author_gate_allowlist.py tests/test_background_job_etiquette_docs.py
Found 9 errors.
No fixes available (3 hidden fixes can be enabled with the `--unsafe-fixes` option).
```

The same 9 findings are then also listed under "Remaining smells (non-auto-fixable)", i.e. they are
counted twice: once as fixed, once as outstanding.

## Root cause (suspected)

`_parse_ruff_fix_output()` in `skill/refactor/scripts/refactor.py` turns **every** JSON entry emitted by
`ruff check --fix --output-format json` into a "fixed finding". Ruff's JSON output after `--fix`
contains the diagnostics that **remain** (those it could not or would not fix, e.g. EXE005/EXE001
shebang/exec bit rules and unsafe-fix candidates), not a ledger of applied fixes. Findings with a
null `fix` field should not be counted as applied.

`_parse_eslint_fix_output()` should be checked for the same assumption.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `_parse_ruff_fix_output()` / `_parse_eslint_fix_output()` count a finding as fixed only when the
   linter actually applied a fix (e.g. ruff entry carries a non-null `fix` payload, or fixes are
   detected by comparing file content before/after the run).
2. A regression test proves that a linter run over files whose remaining diagnostics are
   non-fixable reports `fixes_applied: false` / `Auto-fixed: 0`.
3. A full-project scan of a clean tree leaves `git status` unchanged **and** reports `Auto-fixed: 0`.
4. The "Remaining smells" list is not a duplicate of the auto-fixed list for the same diagnostics.
data.title: Refactor skill reports unfixed linter diagnostics as applied auto-fixes

data.description:
## Goal

Users of the refactor skill need to know whether the project's **tests are
worth keeping**, not only whether the source has code smells. Integrate the
`test-churn` skill into the refactor workflow so every refactor run also
produces test-churn metrics (rewrite ratio, test growth, per-area churn), and
surface that evidence in the refactor skill's final report.

## Problem Statement

The refactor skill currently analyses **source code only** (`refactor.py` scans
`.py`, `.js`, `.jsx`, `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.mjs`, `.cjs`; tests are scanned for
smells like any other code, but their *value* is never assessed). Test-value
evidence exists but only on demand, via the separate `test-churn` skill
(`skill`-external, script `test_churn_analysis.py`). Nothing in the refactor
workflow detects a suite that is growing without manifest benefit, so the
`refactor` run cannot report the pruning signal documented in the test-churn
skill's pruning review workflow.

## User Stories

- **Agent running a refactor:** "When I run the refactor skill, the report tells
  me whether the test suite is growing without benefit, so I can file a
  pruning work item without remembering to run a second skill."
- **Operator / producer:** "Every refactor report carries reproducible test
  churn numbers, so TDD-ROI evidence is produced continuously rather than
  requested ad hoc."
- **Maintainer:** "The integration is additive — a missing/broken test-churn
  script never fails a refactor run, and `--no-churn` restores today's exact
  behaviour."

## Proposed Behaviour

1. `refactor.py` invokes the test-churn analyser as an **additional pipeline
   stage** after smell detection, for both invocation modes (full scan and
   session boundary).
2. A new `--no-churn` flag skips the stage (mirroring `--no-sync`,
   `--no-linter`, `--no-llm`) for offline/deterministic/fast runs.
3. The **human report** gains a test-churn section showing at minimum: modified
   only rewrite ratio, including-new rewrite ratio, net test lines/files
   growth, and the flagged top-churn areas.
4. The **`--json` report** gains a `test_churn` key carrying the analyser's
   `test_churn_data.json` payload (or a documented failure/omitted marker).
5. The stage is **non-fatal**: an unavailable analyser, non-git directory, or
   analyser error logs a warning and the refactor run continues with unchanged
   exit-code semantics (mirroring the existing `wl sync` policy).
6. `SKILL.md` documents the stage, the flag, the report section and the
   non-fatal policy, and cross-references the test-churn skill.

## Constraint: skill boundary

`skill/refactor/` must not import `test_churn_analysis.py` from the installed
skill directory. The integration must resolve the analyser at runtime (the
documented `$(skill_path test-churn)` pattern) or invoke it as a subprocess, so
this repo stays the canonical source and no copy of the analyser is vendored.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: A full-project `/skill:refactor` run renders a test-churn section in the human report containing the modified-only rewrite ratio, the including-new rewrite ratio, and net test line growth.
- [ ] AC2: `refactor.py --json` emits a `test_churn` key whose value contains the analyser metrics (at minimum the two rewrite ratios and `growth_metrics`).
- [ ] AC3: `--no-churn` skips the stage and produces a report byte-identical to current behaviour (no test-churn section, no `test_churn` key).
- [ ] AC4: When the analyser is unavailable or returns non-zero, the run logs a warning, completes successfully, and reports the stage as unavailable — the refactor exit code is unchanged.
- [ ] AC5: `session boundary` mode (`refactor.py <work-item-id>`) also runs the stage, and its work-item `StatusLifecycle` behaviour is unchanged (item never left `in_progress`).
- [ ] AC6: New tests cover the added stage (report rendering, JSON key, `--no-churn`, and the non-fatal failure path) without shelling out to the real analyser — following the test-writing guidelines (no source-grep or self-referential tests).
- [ ] AC7: `skill/refactor/SKILL.md` documents the stage, flag, report section, non-fatal policy and the cross-reference to the test-churn skill.
- [ ] AC8: No code under `skill/refactor/` imports from an installed skill path; the analyser is resolved at runtime or invoked as a subprocess.
- [ ] AC9: Full suite passes (run via the test skill).
data.title: Integrate test-churn analysis into the refactor skill and report

data.description:
## Goal

Make the project's test suite **earn its runtime**: every remaining test should
pin observable behaviour, and no test should exist that cannot fail for a
reason a developer cares about. This epic covers a complete, evidence-led
test-value refactor of the suite — measure, classify, prune, rework, and guard
against reintroduction — rather than the current one-file-at-a-time ad-hoc
cleanups.

## Problem Statement

The suite has grown substantially and carries demonstrable waste:

- **Measured growth (test-churn analyser v2.1.0, `dev` @ 7875214):**
  208,809 test lines added vs 71,787 deleted → **net +137,022 lines**;
  498 test files added vs 114 deleted → **net +384 files**. Net growth is
  positive in **every** calendar quarter, accelerating in 2026-Q3 (+55,892)
  and 2026-Q4 (+38,024).
- **Rewrite ratio is LOW** (14.0% modified-only, 6.2% including new files),
  which means tests largely *survive* feature evolution. That is good news for
  TDD value, but it means growth is dominated by **additive accumulation**,
  not churn — precisely the pattern where dead, duplicated and
  source-grep/structural tests survive unnoticed because nothing forces them
  to be re-examined.
- **Known confirmed offenders found so far:** 5 source-grep / structural
  anti-pattern tests in `tests/unit/test-check-audit-gate.mjs`
  (SA-0MVSCS0M80007X23); 15 test helpers invoking real `git` non-hermetically
  (already tracked, SA-0MUIYHI12000XVM0).
- There is **no standing mechanism** that classifies test files by value, so
  every finding so far depended on a human/agent choosing to look.

## Why an epic (not another leaf)

Value assessment is a repeatable pipeline — detect candidates, prove they no
longer map to behaviour, prune or rework, verify nothing broke, and prevent
reintroduction. That needs coordinated child items across measurement,
classification, remediation, and guarding; single-file items cannot deliver it.

## Existing related work — do NOT duplicate

These items already exist and must be **depended on / coordinated with**, not
recreated:

- `SA-0MVSCS0M80007X23` — rework the 5 source-grep tests in `test-check-audit-gate.mjs`.
- `SA-0MUIYHI12000XVM0` — migrate 15 raw-git test helpers to `git_sandbox` (hermeticity, not value).
- `SA-0MVSCZ2U500420IC` — integrate test-churn metrics into the refactor skill.
- `SA-0MV28WY5Q003N54O` — mutation testing on top-churn modules (evidence arm).
- `SA-0MV28WX8Y005B05G` — prefer interface/behaviour assertions over `toHaveBeenCalledWith` on internal collaborators.
- `SA-0MV28WYLU001BMFU` — scheduled test-churn runs across projects.

## Scope

1. **Measure (baseline).** Capture the test-churn baseline (rewrite ratios, net
   growth, per-area churn, suite wall-clock runtime, per-file runtime) so every
   later change is provable.
2. **Classify.** Run the code-path evaluator (`skill/test/scripts/evaluate_usefulness.py`)
   plus the `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md` anti-pattern checklist
   over the whole suite, recording a **keep / rework / prune** verdict per file.
3. **Prove.** For each prune candidate, demonstrate the behaviour it pins is
   either not observable, already covered elsewhere, or no longer exists
   (`git blame` + coverage grep of the public API). Mutation testing is the
   tie-breaker where provenance is unclear.
4. **Remediate.** Prune dead/duplicate tests; rework devalued ones (source-grep
   → behaviour; placeholder → real assertion or delete; simulation → exercise
   production code).
5. **Guard.** Add a regression guard so the pruned anti-pattern classes cannot
   be reintroduced silently, and so future additions are screened.
6. **Report.** Record before/after metrics so the value delivered is auditable.

## Non-goals

- Not a coverage-maximisation exercise: reducing test count is acceptable and
  expected where tests pin nothing.
- Not a rewrite of the audit/refactor/implement skills' behaviour.
- Not the hermeticity migration (tracked separately in `SA-0MUIYHI12000XVM0`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: A baseline is recorded in this item: modified-only and including-new rewrite ratios, net test file/line growth, suite wall-clock runtime, and the evaluator/checklist verdict for every test file in scope.
- [ ] AC2: Every test file in scope carries an explicit keep / rework / prune verdict with its justifying evidence, and the totals reconcile (verdicts sum to files in scope).
- [ ] AC3: Every prune candidate has written evidence that the behaviour it pinned is not observable, already covered via the public API, or gone — no test is deleted on suspicion alone.
- [ ] AC4: All `prune`-verdict tests are removed and all `rework`-verdict tests are converted to observable-behaviour assertions; no remaining test file reads a source/markdown file and asserts on its text.
- [ ] AC5: After the refactor, `evaluate_usefulness.py` reports no `remove` verdict for any scanned test file, and the suite contains zero placeholder or zero-assertion tests.
- [ ] AC6: The suite is green (full scope, run via the test skill) and no acceptance criterion of any work item loses coverage — demonstrated by the audits and a before/after coverage map, not by assertion counts.
- [ ] AC7: Suite wall-clock runtime is measurably reduced (or, where runtime rises, the item documents why the surviving tests justify it) with before/after numbers.
- [ ] AC8: A regression guard fails the suite if a newly added test matches a pruned anti-pattern class (source-grep, placeholder, zero-assertion, self-referential simulation), without becoming a source-grep test itself.
- [ ] AC9: The pruning workflow in `skill/test-churn/SKILL.md` and the anti-patterns in `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md` are updated with anything this pass learned (new anti-patterns, refined criteria).
- [ ] AC10: Full project test suite passes with the changes, and the final report records the before/after deltas.

## Risks

- **Removing a useful test is a regression; keeping a dead one only costs
  runtime.** Pruning criteria stay conservative — when in doubt, keep the test
  and file a work item.
- Deleting tests can raise apparent coverage drops: coverage is judged by
  behaviour/AC mapping (AC6), never by percentage alone.
- Suite-wide classification is expensive; it must be batched with bounded
  fan-out per the test execution policy (never ad-hoc full suites).

## Notes

Discovered during a test-churn pruning review, 2026-10-28. Priority is medium
because the measured rewrite ratio is already LOW (tests largely survive
feature evolution) — the waste here is accumulation, not thrash, so this is
valuable hygiene rather than an emergency. Children to be created at plan
stage.
data.title: Complete test-value refactor: ensure every test earns its runtime

data.description:
# implement.py Key Files gate misses the bold-inside-heading form

**Discovered from:** RISE-0MVWARX2M001ZXS8 (tce-the-rising implement run, 2026-10-31). That RISE item was filed during `implement.py drive RISE-0MVPAGZP0003EKZU` and is deleted once this item exists (producer decision Q1 = re-file here).

**Headline:** The Key-Files-aware dirty-tree gate in `implement.py` parses only
`## Key Files`, `## Key Files (predicted)` and a bare `**Key Files:**` line, so a
work item whose section is written `## **Key Files:**` (bold marker nested in an
H2/H3) yields no key files, dirty-file relevance becomes unjudgeable, and
`implement.py start` aborts on a dirty checkout even when every dirty path is
unrelated. Make the heading matcher form-agnostic and lock it down with
regression tests.

## Problem statement

`_KEY_FILES_HEADING_RE` in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` matches
`#{1,6}\s*Key Files.*` (heading) **or** `\*\*Key Files:?\*\*.*` (bold line) — but
not the combination `## **Key Files:**`, because after the `## ` prefix the next
token is `**`, not `Key Files`. `extract_key_files_from_description()` then
returns `[]`, `classify_dirty_tree_relevance()` reports *"no Key Files section in
the work item description — cannot judge dirty-file relevance"*, and
`phase_start` takes the conservative abort-and-ask branch even though the
description does list key files and the dirty paths demonstrably do not overlap
them. The gate's conservative default is correct; it is being tripped by a
parser gap rather than by a real risk.

## Evidence

Reproduced in this session against the installed skill tree
(`~/.pi/agent/skills` → `SorraAgents/skill`):

| form | `extract_key_files_from_description` |
|---|---|
| `## Key Files` | `['a/b.ts', 'tests/c.test.ts']` |
| `## Key Files (predicted)` | `['a/b.ts']` |
| `**Key Files:**` | `['a/b.ts']` |
| `## **Key Files:**` | `[]` |
| `### **Key Files:**` | `[]` |

- **Corpus prevalence (consumer store):** 9 of 386 items in the
  `tce-the-rising` store use the bold-inside-heading form — the face-off tie
  epic parent RISE-0MVPAGZP0003EKZU and its eight children
  (RISE-0MVRMI5XD002EDKX, RISE-0MVRMI7GR006QH44, RISE-0MVRMI9F0007HXBW,
  RISE-0MVRMIB7Z008P1HB, RISE-0MVRMID1B0098HAY, RISE-0MVRMIF0T008A72W,
  RISE-0MVRMIGXS0073HDX, RISE-0MVRMIISC009TXYX). For comparison: 297 items use
  a plain heading, 52 a bare bold line, 28 none.
- **Observed stall:** `implement.py drive RISE-0MVPAGZP0003EKZU` aborted on child
  RISE-0MVRMI5XD002EDKX (Key Files: `tests/the-rising/risingMatchHarness.ts`,
  `tests/the-rising/TheRisingRules.test.ts`) although the only dirty paths were
  six untracked `standups/*.md` files — zero overlap, i.e. exactly the
  documented "proceed, leave the dirty files untouched" case. The operator
  worked around it by pre-creating the worktree and running `start` from inside
  it (where the main-checkout gate is skipped by design).
- **No direct test coverage** of `extract_key_files_from_description`,
  `dirty_file_matches_key_files` or `classify_dirty_tree_relevance` exists under
  `skill/implement/tests/`, so this class of gap is invisible to the suite.
- The framework does **not** emit the H2-wrapped form itself:
  `skill/plan/plan_helpers.py` (`_parse_key_files_section`,
  `validate_key_files_format`) and `skill/plan/SKILL.md` use a bare
  `**Key Files:**` line, so both families of form must keep working.

## Users

- **Implement-skill agent (primary)**: "When I start an item whose Key Files
  section is written `## **Key Files:**`, I want `start` to read those paths and
  let me proceed when the dirty files are unrelated, so I do not have to
  hand-work around a gate that already has the information it needs."
- **Producer / operator (secondary)**: "When a downtime run dispatches a child
  session, I want `start` to proceed or abort for a real reason, so unattended
  runs do not stall on a parsing bug."
- **Framework maintainer**: "I want every accepted Key Files heading form
  covered by a table-driven test, so a future edit to the extractor cannot
  silently drop a form."

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1** — `extract_key_files_from_description()` returns the listed paths for
  any `Key Files` heading regardless of emphasis, parenthetical qualifier or
  case: `## **Key Files:**`, `### **Key Files:**`, `## **Key Files (predicted):**`,
  `#### key files`, asserted by a table-driven unit test in
  `skill/implement/tests/`.
- **AC2** — Every currently supported form keeps working, asserted in the same
  table: `## Key Files`, `## Key Files (predicted)`, `### Key Files`, and a bare
  `**Key Files:**` line; plus the tolerant bare-marker variants —
  `  **Key Files:**` (indented/whitespace) and `**Key Files**` (no colon).
- **AC3** — `classify_dirty_tree_relevance()` proceeds (`can_proceed: true`)
  when the description uses `## **Key Files:**` and the dirty paths do not
  overlap those entries, and still aborts (`can_proceed: false`) when a dirty
  path does overlap, or when the description has no Key Files section at all.
- **AC4** — Extraction still stops at the end of the Key Files section: a
  following `#`/`##`/`###` heading or standalone bold section marker terminates
  the list, so prose lines and acceptance-criteria bullets never leak in as
  paths (regression guard for the SA-0MTYMD1NQ009R6W2 defect class).
- **AC5** — A regression test demonstrates the defect before the fix (red on the
  current implementation, green after), and the end-to-end path is verified:
  `implement.py start` on a `## **Key Files:**` item with only unrelated dirty
  paths creates the worktree, leaves the dirty files untouched and records the
  decision in a work-item comment.
- **AC6** — The gate's safety properties are preserved: no
  stash/commit/revert of dirty files, and abort-and-ask still fires for "no Key
  Files section" and for any overlap.
- **AC7** — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes,
  including code comments and docstrings in `implement.py` and the accepted-forms
  list in `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` (Key-Files-aware dirty-tree
  gate, SA-0MV0NSOGE000OSMR) plus the project README and any relevant wiki or
  docs site entries.
- **AC8** — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Scope is `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`** plus its tests and docs
  (producer decision Q2 = A). The two sibling parsers — `skill/plan/plan_helpers.py`
  and `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — are fixed by linked follow-up
  items (below), not here.
- **The gate stays conservative.** No Key Files section, or any overlapping
  dirty path, must still abort and ask. Nothing here may turn the gate into a
  whitelist or relax "never stash/commit/revert the user's work".
- **Must not regress existing forms.** The new matcher may be more tolerant but
  never stricter: an item that starts cleanly today must still start cleanly.
- **Minimal surface.** No new configuration knob or environment variable.
- **UK English** in comments, docstrings and docs.

## Existing state

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`: `_KEY_FILES_HEADING_RE` (~line 1671),
  `extract_key_files_from_description()` (~1676),
  `dirty_file_matches_key_files()` (~1712), `classify_dirty_tree_relevance()`
  (~1742), and the `phase_start` call site (~5993) that turns a
  `can_proceed: false` verdict into the dirty-worktree abort.
- The extractor's loop already terminates on a `#`-heading line or a non-bullet
  line starting with `**`; only the initial heading match is wrong. A new
  matcher must not let the matched heading's own bold marker look like the
  section end.
- `skill/implement/tests/` has suites for the start/finish gates but none that
  exercises the Key Files extractor or the relevance classifier.
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` (Key-Files-aware dirty-tree gate
  section) enumerates the three supported forms and needs the tolerant list.

## Desired change

1. Replace the two-branch heading regex with one form-agnostic matcher: an
   optional H1–H6 prefix, an optional `**` bold marker, `Key Files`, an optional
   parenthetical qualifier and optional closing `**`/`:`, matched
   case-insensitively — while still requiring `Key Files` to be the first
   content token (so `## Notes on Key Files` stays unmatched unless it matches
   today).
2. Keep the section terminator and the bullet/backtick path parsing unchanged
   (including `path → note`).
3. Add the table-driven tests (AC1–AC5) and the end-to-end `start` regression.
4. Update the docstring/comment and `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — form-agnostic `_KEY_FILES_HEADING_RE`,
  extractor terminator/docstrings; classifier branches unchanged.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_key_files_extraction.py` — new table-driven tests
  for the accepted forms, the terminator behaviour and
  `classify_dirty_tree_relevance` proceed/abort decisions.
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — accepted-forms list in the
  Key-Files-aware dirty-tree gate section.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk — over/under-matching:** tightening "first content token" could make a
  heading that matches today (e.g. `## Key Files and notes`) stop matching.
  Keep the match at least as wide as today; assert the old forms in the table.
- **Risk — terminator drift:** after accepting the new form the loop must not
  treat the matched heading's own `**` as a section end.
- **Risk — untestable "it works now" claims:** the AC5 end-to-end check needs a
  deliberately dirty main checkout, so it must leave the dirty files untouched
  and clean up after itself (or exercise the classifier/`phase_start` seam
  directly).
- **Assumption:** the H2-wrapped form is agent-authored markdown, not framework
  output — so the fix belongs in the tolerant parser, not in the plan skill's
  emitter.
- **Scope-creep guard:** the plan/audit parsers are separate items (below);
  anything further discovered goes to `discovered-from` items, not this fix.

- **SA-0MUYEV5AO006V0HK** — project-local skill extensions / dirty-tree

- **SA-0MTYMD1NQ009R6W2** — `plan_helpers._parse_key_files_section` did not stop

- **SA-0MTYP6T2I00396J7** — generated `standups/` output not gitignored: the

- **SA-0MVTOR53E003IIEQ** — the previous framework fix discovered from a

- **RISE-0MVPAGZP0003EKZU** — Face-off tie epic whose children carry the

## Linked follow-up items (producer decision Q2 = B and C)

- **Follow-up 1 — plan parser:** `skill/plan/plan_helpers.py`
  `_parse_key_files_section` / `validate_key_files_format` should accept the same
  heading forms so plan validation does not report a missing/empty Key Files
  section for a validly-written description.
- **Follow-up 2 — audit parser:** `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`'s Key
  Files extraction (`^#{0,4}\s*Key Files.*?$`) has the same blind spot, which
  omits the item's files from the Phase 2 file-scope manifest. Either fix it

Both are filed with `discovered-from:<this item>`; their SA ids are recorded in
